exact_replacements.original:
For a positive integer $n$, define the normalized additive block distortion by

$$d_n(x^n,\widehat x^n):=\frac1n\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}d(x_i,\widehat x_i).$$
exact_replacements.proposed:
For a positive integer $n$ and ordered blocks $x^n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathcal X^n$ and $\widehat x^n=(\widehat x_1,\ldots,\widehat x_n)\in\widehat{\mathcal X}^{\,n}$, define the normalized additive block distortion by

$$d_n(x^n,\widehat x^n):=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^{n}d(x_t,\widehat x_t).$$

If the same ordered blocks are labeled $x_a^{a+n-1}:=(x_a,\ldots,x_{a+n-1})$ and $\widehat x_a^{a+n-1}:=(\widehat x_a,\ldots,\widehat x_{a+n-1})$, for any integer $a$, the equivalent formula is

$$d_n(x_a^{a+n-1},\widehat x_a^{a+n-1})=\frac1n\sum_{i=a}^{a+n-1}d(x_i,\widehat x_i).$$

The substitution $i=a+t-1$ gives the defining sum, so changing the coordinate labels changes neither the block distortion nor its normalization. In particular, blocks $X_0^{n-1}$ use the indices $0,\ldots,n-1$, while blocks $X^n=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ use $1,\ldots,n$.

scientific_rationale: Define x^n as an ordered 1-based tuple, making the IID and WZ interfaces well-defined, and prove by an explicit integer change of index that every consecutively labeled block, including stationary zero-based blocks and random-cut shifted blocks, has its existing average. The original arbitrary measurable alphabets, extended-valued nonnegative single-letter distortion, positive n, expected criterion and strict excess event are retained. Finite nonempty is added only where a real maximum over a finite product is defined; it does not restrict the general distortion domain. No helper item or consumer rewrite is necessary.
